t: Nanak was born into a Hindu Khatri family in Punjab, worked in the state stores at Sultanpur, and, according to Sikh belief, received a divine call in about 1496 after vanishing into the Bein river.
He taught one God, Ik Onkar, the equality of people regardless of gender, caste or religion, and a householder's life of honest work, sharing and remembrance of the divine name.
He settled at Kartarpur, where his community practised communal eating and singing, and he passed the guruship to Bhai Lehna, who became Guru Angad, not to his sons.
dyk: Guru Arjan included 974 hymns by Nanak in the Ādi Granth in 1604, and the Japji forms the opening of the work.
ev: Nanak is born at Rāi Bhoi Dī Talvaṇḍī, now Nankana Sahib
He disappears into the Bein river and returns after three or four days, saying that there is no Hindu and no Muslim
He visits the Sylhet region in Bengal, according to modern accounts
Around the age of 55 he settles at Kartarpur on the Ravi, where the Nanak Panth takes shape
He names Bhai Lehna as Guru Angad and dies at Kartarpur on 22 September
Guru Arjan includes 974 of his hymns in the Ādi Granth

f.born: 15 April 1469, at Rāi Bhoi Dī Talvaṇḍī (now Nankana Sahib, Punjab, Pakistan), a Bedi Khatri; another tradition gives the month of Kārtik (November)
f.died: 22 September 1539, at Kartarpur, aged 70, after naming Bhai Lehna (Guru Angad) as his successor
f.role: First of the ten Sikh gurus; Sikhs regard him as the founder of their faith, and scholars describe him as a poet and teacher in the nirguni tradition of the Bhakti movement
f.known: Teaching Ik Onkar, one God; the Japji Sahib; 974 hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib; the udasis; the settlement at Kartarpur; langar; naam japo, kirat karo and vand chhako
